title: Why Video Processing Matters for the Next Generation of Robots
gist: Mobilint has begun mass production of edge AI chips embedding Chips&Media's video codec IP (VPU claimed 8K60 on a single core, ISO 26262 ASIL-B) targeting multi-camera robots and humanoids. The article flags what is unproven: supported formats at that throughput, production volumes, named robot customers and real multi-stream performance under AI load.

insights.claim: South Korean edge-AI chipmaker Mobilint announced on November 4 that it has begun mass production of next-generation edge AI chips incorporating Chips&Media's video codec technology, targeting robotics including humanoids.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Moves Chips&Media's license relationship into production — potential royalty stream tied to physical AI.

insights.claim: Mobilint licensed H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC and AV1 from Chips&Media and later added AV2 and H.266/VVC; the dedicated VPU is claimed to encode multiple streams and handle 8K at 60 fps on a single core.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Broad codec licensing indicates deepening IP content per chip.

insights.claim: The Mobilint–Chips&Media announcement leaves production volumes, named robot customers, deployment schedules and the formats supported at 8K60 throughput unspecified; commercial traction will only be shown by robot makers choosing the chips and demonstrating sustained camera-plus-inference performance.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Don't price in robotics revenue until design wins with named robot makers appear.

insights.claim: Chips&Media estimates a robot chip may need to handle eight to 20 camera channels simultaneously, with distinct workloads such as low-latency navigation feeds versus efficiently compressed recording for incidents, teleoperation and debugging.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Multi-camera robots expand video-IP and memory-bandwidth content per edge AI chip.
insights.locator: A robot may use forward-facing cameras

insights.claim: Dedicated video-encoding hardware offloads the general-purpose processor, helping battery-powered robots manage power and heat with several feeds active; the practical test is stream count at real resolutions within the power budget while AI models run.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Specialized accelerators (VPU) gain relevance in power-constrained physical-AI SoCs.

insights.claim: Chips&Media's video codec IP carries ISO 26262 ASIL-B automotive functional-safety certification, cited as a reason Mobilint selected it, and the companies plan to explore frame buffer and data compression to relieve memory-bandwidth contention among cameras, encoding and AI inference.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Safety certification and compression IP could be cross-sold from automotive into robotics.
